chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari and Muhammad ibn Yahya, altogether, from al-Husayn ibn Ishaq and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hafs, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no believer who commits a sin except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has appointed for him a respite of seven hours from the day. So if he repents, nothing is written against him, and if he does not (repent), Allah writes one evil deed against him.'

So 'Abbad al-Basri came to him and said to him: 'It has reached us that you said: There is no servant who commits a sin except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has appointed for him a respite of seven hours from the day.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I did not say it like this, but I said: There is no believer,' and that was how my words were.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between 'servant' and 'believer' in the context of the seven-hour respite for repentance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the divine respite of seven hours for repentance after committing a sin is specific to a 'believer' (mu'min), not just any 'servant' (abd). If the believer repents within this time, the sin is erased; otherwise, one evil deed is recorded. This distinction highlights the elevated spiritual status of the mu'min, who is granted a specific window of grace to rectify their state, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interplay between faith and action in the process of tawbah.
